extracted.intended_audience: individuals applying for registration to practice before the USPTO (prospective patent agents/attorneys) and practitioners handling OED petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Administrative standards and procedural requirements for applying for registration to practice before the USPTO (moral character inquiries) and for petitioning the USPTO Director to review an OED Final Decision. Covers substantive character criteria, application certifications, and procedural fee/filing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good moral character and reputation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO requires agents, attorneys, or other persons being recognized as representatives of applicants or other persons, to show that they are of good moral character and reputation prior to registration. (35 U.S.C. §2(b)(2)(D); 37 C.F.R. §11.7(a)(2)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director conducts investigations into moral character and reputation and may deny registration if an applicant fails to demonstrate present possession of good moral character and reputation. The Final Decision standard requires showing present (current) good moral character; past unrelated matters (e.g., failure to pass the exam) may be irrelevant to that inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application truthfulness certification / false statement penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requires applicants to certify that 'each and every statement or representation in this application is true and correct.' The application warns that 'A willfully false statement or certification is a criminal offense and is punishable by law [18 U.S.C. §1001].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must sign and certify accuracy of all statements; willful misstatements can carry criminal penalties. Candor and completeness in the application are material to the registration decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose delinquencies on State or Federal debt
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration application asks whether the applicant was delinquent on any State or Federal debt, including delinquencies from taxes, loans, overpayment of benefits, and defaults on federally guaranteed or insured loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to disclose delinquencies (including federal and state taxes) can bear on assessments of financial responsibility, candor, and moral character. Repeated inconsistent answers across multiple applications are problematic; OED may inquire further or treat nondisclosure as adverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show Cause Requirement scope (financial responsibility and candor)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED may issue a Show Cause Requirement asking the applicant to show cause as to whether there are impediments to concluding the applicant is of good moral character and reputation. The Show Cause Requirement set forth questions about the applicant's financial responsibility, candor, and whether he had satisfactorily established he presently possesses the required good moral character and reputation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must timely respond to Show Cause notices with full explanations and supporting materials; the OED considers those responses as part of its moral character investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on applicant to establish present good moral character
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner has the burden of establishing that he currently possesses the good moral character and reputation as required by 37 C.F.R. §11.7(a)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED will consider all applications, statements, materials, and responses when determining whether the applicant has met the burden. Failure to meet the burden supports denial of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for review must be accompanied by petition fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for review of a Final Decision of the OED Director is required to be accompanied by a petition fee. (37 C.F.R. §§11.2(d) and 1.21(a)(5)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition without payment of the required fee renders the petition incomplete and subject to dismissal. The petition must include payment at time of filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees must be paid in advance at time of requesting action
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. §1.22(a) states that fees are required to be paid in advance, i.e., at the time of requesting any action by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A payment instrument that is returned (e.g., bank cannot locate account) does not satisfy the advance-payment requirement. Applicants should ensure the fee is actually paid (funds honored) when filing requests or petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date is date of receipt absent special procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If the petitioner did not utilize either of the procedures set out in 37 C.F.R. §§1.8 or 1.10, the filing date of the Present Petition is the date of receipt at the USPTO (not the postmark).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To secure an earlier filing date by mail, use the specific procedures in §§1.8 or 1.10; otherwise the Office treats the receipt date as the filing date. Timing rules affect timeliness of petitions and rights to seek review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for nonpayment of petition fee (incompleteness and dismissal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the petitioner had not paid the requisite petition fee (check returned), the petitioner has not satisfied requirements for filing a petition for review under 37 C.F.R. §11.2(d); accordingly, the Present Petition is incomplete and should be dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonpayment (including payment via dishonored check) results in dismissal of a petition as incomplete. Ensure valid, cleared payment accompanies petitions to avoid dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director authority and available review
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director receives and acts on applications for registration, including investigations into moral character and reputation. An individual dissatisfied with the OED Director's final decision may petition the USPTO Director for review under 37 C.F.R. §11.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions by the OED Director are issued as Final Decisions and may be reviewed by the USPTO Director if procedural requirements (including fee payment and timely filing) are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of payment instrument
rubrics_metrics.description: A check enclosed for the petition fee was returned to the USPTO because the bank could not locate the account upon which the check was drawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment instruments must be valid and honored; a returned or dishonored instrument does not constitute payment. Use reliable payment methods to ensure the Office receives funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination performance not determinative of moral character inquiry
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioner's failure to pass the examination after several attempts is not relevant to the issues in this Order and will not be further addressed herein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance on the registration examination itself is distinct from the moral character and reputation inquiry; lack of exam success does not alone justify denial of registration on character grounds.
